Workstream I1 + I2 + I4 (part): origin highlight for parent navigation (opts.origin threaded through navigate/leave; go_parent passes the child name; new ScratchbufOrigin highlight + cursor on the origin row when the current session is not at this level); readably aged liveness markers (live_sessions now fetches '#S|#{session_activity}', new fmt_age helper, ● gets a relative age — now/5m/3h/2d — dead rows stay ○); plus the two new helpers the refresh work needs: close_title (replace a stale board/palette window instead of focusing it; refuses + focuses when the buffer is modified) and an opts.reload hook called by r/<C-l> refresh. current_row now compares folder-qualified names so the "you are here" highlight still works inside folders after I3.

Workstream I3 + I4: folder-scoped session identity (qualified(folder,name) helper; tmux session for folder "block" + name "test" is "block/test", root keeps bare names). open_session, R restart, path recreates and all kill paths (deleted rows, doomed folders) use the qualified name; commit no longer drops same-name sessions from OTHER folders (only same-level duplicates, last edit wins); root "live-only" filter claims rows by qualified name; in_draft/add_to_board are folder-aware. Legacy bare live session with a folder row is adopted by rename-session on board open (idempotent migration, slot file updated) and again on W for rows that appear later; never steals a bare name another row claims. I4: open_workboard now does refresh_from_disk + invalidate_live + migrate + load_draft on every open, replaces a stale open board via browser.close_title (bails with a warning when the board has unsaved edits), and passes an opts.reload hook so r/<C-l> also re-read the store; open_prefix matching uses qualified names. (+) saves the row to the palette under its qualified name; "R" restarts the qualified session and shows it in the confirm prompt.

Workstream I4: new M.refresh_from_disk() re-reads tmux_project_overrides.json and replaces M.projects/M.workspaces/M.board in memory, reusing read_store and ordered_group_names (project order preserved for still-existing groups). This is the store half of "opening leader>ts always shows the current state": the board calls it before every open/reload, and the palette calls it on every open, so writes from other nvim instances are never invisible. Missing/invalid file keeps memory untouched (returns false).

I4 parity for the palette + workspace handoff coherence with I3. pick_project now calls M.refresh_from_disk() and replaces a stale palette window via browser.close_title({ "Tmux Palette", "Palette" }) — same unsaved-edits guard as the board (focus + warn instead of discarding). open_workspace creates sessions under their folder-qualified tmux name and hands them off with their folder, so workspace launches land in the right folder instead of producing bare-named duplicates that would never match a folder row. Palette folder semantics (name-global uniqueness) are intentionally unchanged — the palette remains the global namespace; changes here stay at the open/launch boundary.

Both refresh entry points share a reload_state() wrapper that reports a failing store reload via notification and still refreshes instead of aborting the keypress silently. decorate() gains a buffer-validity guard because it can now be invoked from a scheduled (deferred) callback.

Refresh completeness, panel side (follow-up to accepted FINAL-11): the A/O hidden-session panels' refresh function listed from the cached browser.live_sessions() without invalidating it, so r / <C-l> could never surface newly created air/opencode sessions in a refreshed panel (and left the board's cache stale too). No other behavior changed.

Refresh completeness, palette side (follow-up to accepted FINAL-10): the palette only re-read the store on open, so pressing r / <C-l> inside the palette refreshed the live tmux state but kept showing a stale store — palette edits made by another nvim instance stayed invisible until the palette was closed and reopened. Added the reload hook so the palette's refresh now calls M.refresh_from_disk(), matching the board. No other behavior changed.

Tab UX fixes from your report: (1) the insert-mode Tab mapping is removed entirely — it was intercepting Tab while typing rows and blocking nvim-cmp, and is what closed the completion/window you expected; with no mapping, a bare Tab in insert mode inserts the separator character itself (fixing "path glues onto the name") or drives nvim-cmp when its menu is open. (2) Normal-mode Tab now genuinely opens the path part: on a row with no separator yet it appends the TAB separator and parks the cursor after it, instead of silently doing nothing and letting the path text merge into the name. (3) Hop logic refined: name -> path, path -> name, no jump while the path is still empty, no-op on folder rows.

Rows are pointers — creating and copying rows must never delete or hijack a session. Two changes: (1) silent (navigation) commits no longer kill tmux sessions; only an explicit save (W) that removes a row or folder kills. Previously, cutting a row and navigating into the target folder (i.e. any dd/gp move or copy-paste flow) committed the source level and killed the session there — that was the "delete another" you hit when creating a row with the same cwd/name as an existing session. (2) The W-time adoption rename is removed: saving a row never renames or adopts a running bare-named session anymore. The guarded one-time migration of legacy stored rows on board open stays. Net effect: you can create any row with any name and any cwd (including a cwd an existing session uses), copy rows between folders keeping the same name (folder-qualified names make them distinct sessions) or renaming them, and nothing else is touched. Deleting a row/folder and pressing W still kills it, as before.

Same pointer rules in the palette: (1) removed the cross-folder same-name drop — creating "test" in one palette folder no longer deletes "test" from another; folders are independent lists and a shared name resolves to the same tmux session, so you can copy a definition into another folder under the same or a new name. (2) Kills now happen only on explicit save: row deletions and folder removals (delete_tree) kill their session only when W commits; navigating folders never kills anything. Launching/handing off to the board is unchanged.

Fix for the "displaying weird again" view: those rows (terraform/foundation, volleyball/foundation, volleyball/terraform-staging, terraform/volleyball/terraform-staging) are orphaned live sessions — their rows were moved/deleted and, per the new pointer rules, the sessions survived with nothing pointing at them, so the root showed them under raw qualified names. Three changes: (1) adopt_orphans() runs on every board open/reload: a live "<folder>/<name>" session with no row is homed into the longest existing board-folder prefix of its name (row added with the live path, folder untouched, no folders invented, idempotent, notifies the count) — your four orphaned sessions will land back inside terraform/ and volleyball/ with ● instead of cluttering the root. (2) Opening a session from a folder row now persists that row as a pointer (previously a row created and opened without W was lost and the session became a root orphan). (3) The + palette save stores the bare name plus the board folder it came from, so relaunching from the palette lands the session back in its folder instead of making a qualified-name root row.

Palette side of the orphan fix: entries saved from the board with + now carry the board folder they came from, and launching such an entry hands that folder to the board (add_to_board(name, path, folder)) so the session lands back inside its folder with its bare name — instead of creating a root row with a qualified name like "terraform/foundation". The folder field survives palette edits (carried from the previous entry on commit). No other palette behavior changed.
